title: Marketing to sales handoff: A B2B checklist and example
summary: Build a clear marketing to sales handoff with a B2B checklist, sample agreement, and examples for lead ownership and follow-up.
body_markdown:
A marketing to sales handoff gives a named salesperson responsibility for following up with a lead. Both teams need to agree on which leads to transfer and what information sales needs. The process also needs a way to record the sales decision and next action.


A demo request might arrive with a name and email address, but the salesperson still needs context. What did the person ask for? Does someone already own the account? What did marketing promise? Those details belong in the record sales will use to respond.


The checklist and sample agreement below give B2B teams a process to adapt to their own business.


## What happens during a marketing to sales handoff?


Once a lead meets the team’s transfer criteria, it moves through assignment and review. The handoff ends when someone records the decision and takes responsibility for the next action.


Keep these three decisions separate:


Decision What it means


Marketing qualifies the lead for transfer The lead meets agreed criteria for sales review


Sales accepts the lead A salesperson agrees to take responsibility for working it


Sales qualifies an opportunity Further assessment establishes that the lead meets the team’s requirements for a potential deal


Adapt these working definitions to your business. A salesperson can accept responsibility for a demo request while purchasing authority and budget remain unknown.


[HubSpot’s lifecycle documentation](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/records/use-lifecycle-stages) distinguishes marketing-qualified leads from sales-qualified leads and opportunities. Your CRM labels may differ; document what each means in your process.


For the roles involved, see our guide to[GTM team roles and structure](https://blog.floworks.ai/gtm-team-roles-structure/) .


## 1. Agree on which leads should reach sales


Write criteria that someone in either team can check against the lead record. Assess account fit separately from what the person has done.


Account fit might include the industries you serve, supported locations, company size, or a relevant use case. Engagement might include a demo request, a pricing inquiry, or an explicit request to discuss a problem.


Then decide where each type of inquiry goes. For example:


- A demo request from an account in your target market goes to sales for review.
- A relevant contact who downloads an educational resource stays with marketing unless another agreed condition triggers transfer.
- An existing customer’s inquiry goes to its account owner.
- A support request goes to the support team.


Adapt these example rules to your qualification process. A content download alone does not confirm a buying project.


Keep the criteria consistent with your[ideal customer profile](https://blog.floworks.ai/ideal-customer-profile-template/) , and specify who resolves exceptions. Make sure someone responds to direct requests for a conversation, even when account details are incomplete.


## 2. Prepare the lead handoff checklist


Choose the required fields for each lead type so the salesperson can respond without piecing together the inquiry:


Information What to record


Contact and account Name, available contact details, company, and domain


Source Campaign, referral, form, or other source, with a date


Reason for transfer The specific condition the lead met


Request or problem The person’s own words where available; distinguish these from research notes


Relevant activity What happened and when, with a link to the underlying record


Previous contact Existing account owner, open opportunity, or recent conversation


Contact preferences Any stated channel preference, requested contact time, or instruction not to contact


Ownership and timing Assigned salesperson, assignment time, and follow-up deadline


Leave unknowns clearly marked. A job title may identify a relevant contact; confirming that person’s role in a purchase requires more evidence.


For direct inquiries, decide what you need before responding and what can be researched afterward. Someone can acknowledge a demo request while the team fills in the technology profile.


## 3. Assign an owner and a fallback


Document the routing order, including how to resolve conflicting assignments. One approach is to check for an existing account owner or open opportunity first, then apply territory, segment, or team-assignment rules.


Give each routed lead a named owner. If leads enter a queue first, someone needs to monitor it and resolve unassigned records.


Write down what happens when an owner is absent, routing information is missing, or the inquiry duplicates an existing record. Include when a manager steps in and who handles urgent requests outside normal coverage.


Keep the original assignment time through reassignment so an overdue inquiry cannot appear new.


## 4. Write a handoff agreement both teams can use


A service-level agreement, or SLA, records the commitments marketing and sales make to each other.[Salesforce’s alignment guide](https://www.salesforce.com/marketing/sales-marketing-alignment/) recommends documenting qualification criteria, follow-up timeframes, and feedback on disqualified leads.[HubSpot Academy](https://academy.hubspot.com/lessons/holding-your-teams-accountable-with-a-service-level-agreement) also treats the SLA as a way to establish accountability between the teams.


The sample agreement uses illustrative deadlines. They are not response-time benchmarks; choose timings that fit your staffing, lead types, and customer expectations.


Agreement item Example rule


Scope New-business demo requests from accounts meeting the agreed fit criteria


Marketing commitment Record the request, source, available contact details, and reason for transfer; resolve missing required information


Volume planning Review expected inquiry volume against sales capacity; record an agreed volume commitment if appropriate


Sales owner The assigned account or territory salesperson, with a named backup


Coverage Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. America/New_York time


Review deadline Record acceptance, return, or redirection within two business hours of assignment


First-response deadline Make the first personal response within four business hours of assignment, unless the person requests a later time


Clock rules Count covered business hours; preserve assignment time through reassignment


Exceptions Route missing-owner or overdue records to the sales manager; record exceptions and their reasons


Feedback Every returned lead needs a reason and a named next owner


Measure review and response separately. An automated receipt acknowledges the submission; a personal response addresses the person’s request. Specify which event counts in your report.


## 5. Record what happens after sales reviews the lead


Record what sales decided and what happens next. These outcomes distinguish suitability from work still in progress:


- Accepted: sales owns follow-up, with a next action and due date.
- Returned for nurturing: the account may fit, but the conversation is not appropriate yet; record the reason and a review condition.
- Needs correction: required information is missing or inaccurate; assign responsibility for fixing it.
- Redirected: another account owner or department should respond.
- Disqualified: a documented reason makes the lead unsuitable for the current sales process.


After the agreed follow-up process, record no response as its own outcome. A lack of response alone does not establish poor account fit.


Avoid a catch-all reason such as “bad lead.” More useful notes say “existing customer assigned to account team” or “requested educational updates only; no sales conversation requested.”


When a lead returns to marketing, state what would trigger another transfer. A new demo request or a reply asking to revisit the discussion might qualify, along with any other agreed changes. Keep the history available to the next salesperson.


## A B2B handoff example


This example uses a fictional company and fictional people to show the process in practice. It does not describe Floworks customer results.


A B2B software company sells a reporting product to operations teams. Its marketing and sales teams agree that a demo request from an account meeting their fit criteria should receive sales review. Educational downloads alone remain with marketing.


### Lead one: a request sales accepts


Priya, an operations manager at a suitable account, submits a demo request. She writes: “We combine reports manually and want to see whether your product supports our reporting process.”


Marketing records the submission and checks for an existing owner. The lead goes to Alex, the salesperson responsible for that account segment.


Handoff field Recorded information


Reason for transfer Demo request from an account meeting the agreed fit criteria


Stated problem Manual work combining reports


Requested next step Product demonstration


Unknowns Budget, purchasing authority, other stakeholders, and decision timing


Sales decision Accepted for follow-up


Next action Alex responds to arrange the demonstration and clarify reporting needs


Alex now owns the follow-up. The company still needs further conversation to establish whether the lead meets its requirements for a qualified opportunity.


### Lead two: a contact returned for nurturing


Jordan works at another account that fits the target market and downloads a reporting checklist. A campaign rule sends the record to sales, even though downloads alone should not trigger transfer.


Sales returns it with the reason: “Educational download only; transfer criteria not met.” Marketing becomes the next owner for any appropriate nurturing and corrects the campaign rule. A later demo request would trigger a fresh review.


Keep the mistaken transfer in the audit history so both teams can see the routing problem.


## How to measure lead handoff quality


Follow the same group of handed-off leads through the report. Finalize each rate only after its full measurement window has passed, and show pending records separately.


Measure Suggested calculation or check


Sales acceptance rate Leads accepted within the defined review window ÷ All leads handed off in that cohort × 100


Review deadline compliance Leads with a recorded review decision by their deadline ÷ Handed-off leads whose review deadline has passed × 100


First-response compliance Applicable accepted leads personally contacted by their original response deadline ÷ Applicable accepted leads whose response deadline has passed × 100


Handoff-to-opportunity conversion Handed-off leads that produce a qualified opportunity within the chosen window ÷ All handed-off leads in that cohort × 100


Define which records you exclude from response reporting, such as inquiries redirected to support or instructions not to contact. Show those counts beside the rate. Read response compliance alongside acceptance and review compliance: quick responses to accepted leads can coexist with a queue nobody has reviewed.


Count each handed-off lead once in the opportunity-conversion calculation and document how leads are associated with opportunities. Report unique opportunities separately when several contacts belong to one deal.


Break down return reasons by source and segment. More records needing correction calls for a different investigation from more accounts failing the fit criteria. Keep qualification definitions consistent across this report and your wider GTM reporting.


## Where Jesse fits into preparation


[Jesse, a product of Floworks](https://agentjesse.ai/) , supports company and people search, contact enrichment, and finding contacts by selected roles. Teams can use these capabilities to research account details for a handoff record.


Distinguish company research from what the prospect has said. Use the research as context and check the evidence needed for your qualification decision.


For example, a researched company profile may help check account fit, while the person’s demo request explains why sales should respond. Record assignment, acceptance, and follow-up in the system your team uses to manage the handoff.


## Frequently asked questions


### Is every MQL ready for an opportunity?


No. A lead may meet the criteria for transfer and be accepted for follow-up while sales is still gathering the evidence needed to qualify an opportunity.


### How quickly should sales follow up?


Choose targets for each inquiry type based on coverage hours and capacity. Write down when the clock starts and what counts as a response, including how you handle after-hours requests. The deadlines in this guide are examples.


### Can a small team use a handoff agreement?


Yes. Keep a short shared document covering transfer criteria, required information, ownership, and returns. Even when one person covers several roles, each lead needs a clear next action.


### What should marketing do with a rejected lead?


Start with the recorded reason. The next step might be correcting information, redirecting an existing customer, or returning a suitable account to nurturing. Keep disqualified contacts from automatically entering sales follow-up again after a routine campaign interaction.
